children: Goldman Sachs is sharply raising its outlook for
diesel refining margins
, signaling that the global fuel squeeze could persist well into 2027 and deliver another earnings tailwind for refiners such as
Marathon Petroleum
, Valero Energy
and
Phillips 66
. The bank more than doubled its forecasts as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine disrupt refining capacity, tighten inventories and keep diesel prices elevated.

A refining margin, or crack spread, measures the difference between the cost of crude oil and the value of products refiners produce from it. Wider spreads generally translate into stronger refinery profits, making Goldman's dramatic forecast increase particularly important for energy-stock investors.
Diesel remains at the epicenter of the rally, Goldman said. The bank now expects the profit from producing a barrel of diesel over Brent crude to average
$63 per barrel in the U.S. and $49 in Europe next year
, sharply above its previous forecasts of
, respectively.
The supply squeeze is unusually severe. Goldman said refinery outages are running
60% above seasonal norms
, while inventories continue falling. Russia, normally the world's second-largest diesel exporter, has extended its diesel export ban through
September 30
after Ukrainian attacks disrupted domestic refineries.
Middle Eastern disruptions are compounding the shortage. Asian refined-fuel imports fell to
5.1 million barrels per day in August
, roughly 2 million barrels below pre-war levels, while diesel refining margins in Singapore have tripled since the conflict began.
Goldman warned that a full recovery in runs requires global geopolitical deescalation.
Investors Takeaway
For refiners, investors should track
diesel crack spreads, refinery utilization rates, inventories and Russian export policy
. Persistently elevated margins could continue supporting outsized cash flow and shareholder returns; Phillips 66 recently expanded its share-repurchase authorization by
$10 billion
amid stronger refining economics.

The biggest downside catalyst is geopolitical de-escalation that restores Russian and Middle Eastern fuel exports. Until then, tight diesel supply could remain bullish for refiners while adding another inflationary pressure point for transportation, manufacturing and consumers.

title: Goldman Sachs Sees Major Shift Coming for Oil Markets
